requirement_text.ISS-0216: Letflow.Api.Pagination.decode_cursor/4 trusted its caller-supplied prefix with no non-empty guard -- check_prefix/2's size/starts_with? logic trivially passes when prefix is the empty string, since every decoded cursor starts with the empty string, defeating the cross-endpoint cursor isolation this parameter exists to provide.

result.summary:
Reviewed git diff main...HEAD on lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex (single commit 2b0d881, +39/-0 lines net on this file: a new leading defp check_prefix/2 clause for prefix == "" that raises ArgumentError with a detailed message, plus moduledoc INV-9 paragraph and @doc prose on decode_cursor/4). Also re-ran verification independently rather than trusting SECURITY-REVIEWER's quoted output: mix format --check-formatted lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex -> exit 0; mix compile --warnings-as-errors -> exit 0, no warnings; mix test test/letflow/api/pagination_test.exs -> 'Finished in 0.1 seconds ... Result: 38 passed', 0 failures.

1. Idiomatic vs. crutch -- N/A to gen_statem/GenServer concerns: Letflow.Api.Pagination is a pure, stateless encode/decode module (moduledoc states explicitly: no Ecto.Schema/Repo, no Plug.Conn dependency), not a process. The fix itself is idiomatic Elixir: a pattern-matched defp clause (check_prefix(_decoded, "")) placed before the general clause, using Elixir's standard 'raise on caller-contract violation vs. return tagged tuple on payload validation' convention (the same shape as Keyword.fetch!/2, Map.fetch!/2) -- not a hand-rolled cond/case doing dispatch that pattern matching should do. No crutch found.

2. Supervision -- N/A. No process, no Letflow.InstanceSupervisor-managed instance, no spawn, no shared state introduced. This module has no supervision tree footprint at all; nothing to collapse or isolate.

3. Type-safety gaps -- considered and deliberately not filed. The invalid state (prefix == "") is a String.t() value-level precondition, not a type-level distinction Elixir's type system (or Dialyzer, which is structural/success-typing, not refinement-typed) can make unrepresentable without introducing a wrapper type (e.g. a NonEmptyString.t() opaque struct) for a single internal defp argument that is never part of the public API surface exposed to a wider caller set beyond this module's own six hardcoded call-site literals (verified in SECURITY-REVIEWER's step-03b: audit.ex, tenants.ex, identity.ex, tasks.ex, instances.ex, definitions.ex all pass compile-time @-attribute literals, never derived values). Introducing a custom non-empty-string type here for one defp guard would itself be scope creep relative to ISS-0216's narrow fix -- not a gap worth an issue. No docs/issues/ entry filed; this determination is recorded here per the reviewer instructions' intent (an observation that a type change would help, weighed and rejected as disproportionate to this fix, not left silently unrecorded).

4. Scope creep -- none found. The diff is exactly the fix ISS-0216 called for: one new pattern-matched defp clause, plus documentation (moduledoc INV-9 paragraph, @doc prose) directly describing that new invariant. No new abstraction (behaviour, macro, generic plumbing), no unrelated refactor, no touching of the five other decode/encode functions in the module. This matches the code-design-validator's already-approved design (lib/letflow/design/iss0216-pagination-prefix-guard.md) with no drift.

docs/anti-patterns.md check: read in full; no entry applies to this diff (entries on file are about timestamp/handoff bookkeeping discipline and requirement-status file handling, not about API/pagination code).

Decision-record consistency: no docs/migration/decisions/ record is implicated by this change (no framework/library choice made or touched).

No blocker. PASS.
